quests.question: ____ you are already familiar with the software, training will only take half a day.
quests.sentence: ____ you are already familiar with the software, training will only take half a day.
quests.hint: 'Since' here means 'because' - the familiarity is the reason for shorter training.
quests.explanation: 'Since' used causally at the start of a sentence introduces a known fact as the reason for what follows. 'Since you are already familiar' = 'because you already know the software'. This is more formal and assumed than 'because'.

quests.question: The final draft reads well, ____ several passages could still be tightened.
quests.sentence: The final draft reads well, ____ several passages could still be tightened.
quests.hint: A well-written draft and passages that need tightening are in mild contrast.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive qualification. The draft reads well (positive) - although some passages could be improved (qualifier). 'Although' here is used mid-sentence to add a nuance without negating the main positive point.

quests.question: Traditional retailers rely on physical footfall, ____ online competitors depend entirely on digital traffic.
quests.sentence: Traditional retailers rely on physical footfall, ____ online competitors depend entirely on digital traffic.
quests.hint: Two competing business models with opposite customer acquisition methods are contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal, balanced contrast between two opposing systems. Physical footfall (traditional) versus digital traffic (online) are placed side by side in a formal comparison of two competing retail approaches.

quests.question: She agreed to the proposal, ____ she had reservations about two specific clauses.
quests.sentence: She agreed to the proposal, ____ she had reservations about two specific clauses.
quests.hint: Her agreement despite genuine reservations is the key tension here.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' is stronger than 'although' - it emphasises that the reservations were real and significant. 'She agreed EVEN THOUGH she had reservations' stresses the weight of her concerns and makes the agreement more surprising.

quests.question: ____ the cost of renewable energy has fallen dramatically, adoption rates remain lower than expected.
quests.sentence: ____ the cost of renewable energy has fallen dramatically, adoption rates remain lower than expected.
quests.hint: Falling costs should drive higher adoption - but it hasn't happened as expected.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession at the start. Falling costs (positive development) would normally drive adoption, but rates remain low (unexpected outcome). 'Although' captures this gap between expectation and reality.

quests.question: He decided to speak plainly, ____ a more diplomatic approach might have caused less offence.
quests.sentence: He decided to speak plainly, ____ a more diplomatic approach might have caused less offence.
quests.hint: He chose plain speaking even though a diplomatic approach was available.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive alternative. A diplomatic approach (available option) would have caused less offence (better outcome), yet he chose plain speaking. 'Although' acknowledges the better option existed but was not taken.

quests.question: ____ the candidate performed exceptionally well, the hiring committee still had concerns.
quests.sentence: ____ the candidate performed exceptionally well, the hiring committee still had concerns.
quests.hint: Exceptional performance and ongoing concerns are in strong tension.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the strength of the concession. Exceptional performance (very strong positive) would normally remove all concerns - 'even though' signals that the concerns persist DESPITE this impressive performance. Stronger than 'although'.

quests.question: The public version of the report is accessible to all, ____ the internal version remains classified.
quests.sentence: The public version of the report is accessible to all, ____ the internal version remains classified.
quests.hint: Two versions with opposite accessibility status are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal, balanced contrast. Public report (accessible to all) versus internal report (classified) - 'whereas' places these two contrasting access levels side by side in a formal, official register.

quests.question: The results were strong in the first quarter, ____ performance declined sharply in the second.
quests.sentence: The results were strong in the first quarter, ____ performance declined sharply in the second.
quests.hint: Two consecutive quarters with opposite performance trends are contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Although' contrasts the strong first quarter with the weaker second. 'Although the first quarter was strong, performance declined in the second' - 'although' shows the positive did not continue, introducing a disappointing contrast.

quests.question: She refuses to compromise on quality, ____ her competitors frequently cut corners.
quests.sentence: She refuses to compromise on quality, ____ her competitors frequently cut corners.
quests.hint: Her commitment to quality and her competitors' corner-cutting are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal contrast between her approach and her competitors'. Her refusal to compromise (one approach) versus their corner-cutting (opposite approach) - 'whereas' makes this a formal side-by-side comparison.

quests.question: He continued to advocate for the policy ____ it had been officially rejected.
quests.sentence: He continued to advocate for the policy ____ it had been officially rejected.
quests.hint: Continuing to advocate after official rejection is particularly surprising.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the weight of the concession. Official rejection (very strong barrier) would normally end advocacy - 'even though' shows he persisted DESPITE this significant formal obstacle. Stronger than 'although'.

quests.question: ____ she had limited resources, she managed to launch a highly successful campaign.
quests.sentence: ____ she had limited resources, she managed to launch a highly successful campaign.
quests.hint: Limited resources are an acknowledged obstacle - but success followed anyway.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive fact at the start. Limited resources (obstacle) would normally prevent a successful campaign, but she succeeded - 'although' shows the obstacle did not prevent the positive outcome.

quests.question: Junior employees are expected to follow the dress code strictly, ____ senior managers have considerably more discretion.
quests.sentence: Junior employees are expected to follow the dress code strictly, ____ senior managers have considerably more discretion.
quests.hint: Two levels of the hierarchy with different dress code expectations are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal contrast between two groups in an organisation. Strict rules (juniors) versus discretion (seniors) - 'whereas' makes this a balanced, formal contrast that highlights the institutional double standard.

quests.question: The committee approved the budget, ____ two members had formally objected.
quests.sentence: The committee approved the budget, ____ two members had formally objected.
quests.hint: Approval despite formal objections from within the committee is notable.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the significance of the internal opposition. Formal objections from committee members (strong internal barrier) would normally prevent or delay approval - 'even though' shows approval happened despite this significant opposition.

quests.question: She accepted less pay for the role ____ she believed in the organisation's mission.
quests.sentence: She accepted less pay for the role ____ she believed in the organisation's mission.
quests.hint: 'Since' here means 'because' - her belief is the reason for accepting lower pay.
quests.explanation: 'Since' used causally means 'because'. 'She accepted less pay since she believed in the mission' = 'she accepted less pay because she believed'. 'Since' (causal) is appropriate when the reason is presented as a known or established fact.

quests.question: The experiment confirmed the hypothesis, ____ one anomalous data point remained unexplained.
quests.sentence: The experiment confirmed the hypothesis, ____ one anomalous data point remained unexplained.
quests.hint: An overall confirmation but with one unexplained anomaly - a minor qualification.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a minor qualification to an otherwise positive result. The hypothesis was confirmed (main result) - although one anomaly remained (minor qualification). 'Although' acknowledges the imperfection without undermining the main finding.

quests.question: Classical economists favour free markets, ____ Keynesian economists argue for state intervention.
quests.sentence: Classical economists favour free markets, ____ Keynesian economists argue for state intervention.
quests.hint: Two opposing economic schools with contrasting policy prescriptions are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' is ideal for a formal, academic contrast between two competing schools of thought. Classical (free markets) versus Keynesian (state intervention) - 'whereas' places these two positions in a formal, balanced academic comparison.

quests.question: ____ she lacked formal qualifications, her practical experience more than compensated.
quests.sentence: ____ she lacked formal qualifications, her practical experience more than compensated.
quests.hint: Lacking qualifications is a potential barrier - but experience made up for it.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive fact at the start. Lacking qualifications (barrier) would normally prevent progression, but experience compensated - 'although' shows the barrier was overcome by an alternative strength.

quests.question: He failed to mention the risks in his presentation, ____ they were clearly documented in the report.
quests.sentence: He failed to mention the risks in his presentation, ____ they were clearly documented in the report.
quests.hint: Failing to mention clearly documented risks is particularly notable and problematic.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the significance of the omission. The risks were clearly documented (very clear availability) - 'even though' shows the omission was more notable because the information was so readily available.

quests.question: ____ the two studies used different methodologies, their conclusions were remarkably similar.
quests.sentence: ____ the two studies used different methodologies, their conclusions were remarkably similar.
quests.hint: Different methods leading to similar conclusions is an interesting and surprising finding.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive contrast. Different methodologies (expected source of different conclusions) led to similar findings (unexpected similarity) - 'although' highlights this surprising convergence.

quests.question: The northern office reports to London, ____ the southern office has its own autonomous structure.
quests.sentence: The northern office reports to London, ____ the southern office has its own autonomous structure.
quests.hint: Two offices with opposite reporting structures are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal, balanced organisational contrast. Centralised reporting (north) versus autonomous structure (south) - 'whereas' places these two different management arrangements in a formal, side-by-side comparison.

quests.question: The charity continued its operations ____ funding had been reduced by forty per cent.
quests.sentence: The charity continued its operations ____ funding had been reduced by forty per cent.
quests.hint: A forty-percent funding cut is a very significant barrier - yet operations continued.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the weight of the financial obstacle. A forty-percent funding reduction (very significant barrier) would normally force cuts or closure - 'even though' shows the charity maintained operations despite this major financial setback.

quests.question: Some investors welcome market volatility, ____ others find it deeply unsettling.
quests.sentence: Some investors welcome market volatility, ____ others find it deeply unsettling.
quests.hint: Two groups of investors with opposite reactions to the same market condition are contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal contrast between two opposite investor responses. Welcoming volatility (some investors) versus finding it unsettling (others) - 'whereas' frames this as a balanced, formal contrast between two groups.

quests.question: ____ the data supports this interpretation, alternative explanations cannot be ruled out.
quests.sentence: ____ the data supports this interpretation, alternative explanations cannot be ruled out.
quests.hint: Supporting data and remaining alternative explanations are in scientific tension.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a scientific qualification. The data supports the interpretation (main finding) - although alternative explanations remain possible (important qualifier). 'Although' acknowledges the strength of the finding while maintaining appropriate scientific caution.

quests.question: He agreed to present at the conference ____ it meant travelling abroad for the first time.
quests.sentence: He agreed to present at the conference ____ it meant travelling abroad for the first time.
quests.hint: First-time international travel can be daunting - agreeing despite this is notable.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the personal challenge involved. Travelling abroad for the first time (significant personal challenge) would normally cause hesitation - 'even though' shows he agreed DESPITE this challenging personal first.

quests.question: The oral exam is assessed on communication skills, ____ the written paper tests analytical reasoning.
quests.sentence: The oral exam is assessed on communication skills, ____ the written paper tests analytical reasoning.
quests.hint: Two assessment components measuring completely different skills are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal, balanced academic contrast. Communication skills (oral) versus analytical reasoning (written) - 'whereas' is the ideal connector for a formal, parallel comparison of two assessment components.

quests.question: She chose the longer, more scenic route ____ the motorway would have been significantly faster.
quests.sentence: She chose the longer, more scenic route ____ the motorway would have been significantly faster.
quests.hint: Choosing the scenic route when a faster option exists is a deliberate, notable choice.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasises the sacrifice involved. A faster motorway (significant advantage) was available - 'even though' shows she chose the slower, more beautiful route DESPITE this clear time-saving alternative.

quests.question: The panel praised his research methodology, ____ they questioned several of his conclusions.
quests.sentence: The panel praised his research methodology, ____ they questioned several of his conclusions.
quests.hint: Praise for methodology but questions about conclusions is a mixed academic review.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concessive qualification. The methodology was praised (positive) - although conclusions were questioned (qualification). 'Although' acknowledges both the strength and the weakness of the academic work.

quests.question: Generation X tends to value job stability, ____ millennials often prioritise work-life balance.
quests.sentence: Generation X tends to value job stability, ____ millennials often prioritise work-life balance.
quests.hint: Two generations with different workplace priorities are formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' provides a formal, balanced generational contrast. Job stability (Generation X) versus work-life balance (millennials) - 'whereas' makes this a formal, side-by-side comparison of different generational workplace values.

quests.question: ____ there is no precedent for this, the court must develop new legal principles.
quests.sentence: ____ there is no precedent for this, the court must develop new legal principles.
quests.hint: 'Since' here means 'because' - the lack of precedent is the reason for developing new principles.
quests.explanation: 'Since' used causally at the start introduces the factual reason for the conclusion. 'Since there is no precedent' = 'because no precedent exists'. The absence of precedent (reason) necessitates creating new principles (conclusion).
